column1: # Game profile of Kirby and the Forgotten Land (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.1.0 = v65536). Plays on Android (android.tsv)
# HAL Laboratory's own engine on NintendoWare (G3d, Font, Fxt) with nn::atk2 sound, SDK 11.4.0 (the sdk build is Pokémon Legends: Arceus's), NVN; subsdk0 is the SDK's movie
# library (VP9 / Vorbis WebM: the opening and ending movies, mov/EventMovie, and the guide movies, mov/GuideMovie). Checked on the device: the build IDs of the three modules,
# the NPDM's system resource (none) and the heap the game sets ("[mem] heap 3.14 GB (heap region 3.25 GB)")
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk0 (the movie library, which main imports from), sdk
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: it sets a heap of the pool less 64 MB of used memory, 3.14 GB, in the 3.25 GB heap region of
# a 4 GB block (256 MB in front, a 256 MB alias region, a 256 MB stack region). The application pool is the Switch's 3285 MB. It grows with each new area: the most of any game here
# 27,297 shaders, BNSH in HAL's .cmp containers (a u32 size, then one zstd or LZ4 frame: shader_split.py unsized) under gfx/ (models, 18,476), ptcl/ (effects, 8,313, 70 of
# them compute), lyt/ (layouts, 387), in the loose shader/ files (67) and in main (54). Without opening the containers the split finds only the 121 outside them
